text:
joan: Quick sync 1: QA says the undo affordance for rollbacks is hard to find when the toast disappears. Thoughts on toast vs timeline placement?
ryan: I'm +1 to keep Undo in timeline (with modal) and make toast link to that entry. Toasts are transient and we shouldn't cram critical actions there.
marta: Agreed. But we should make the toast more actionable: short copy + 'View history' CTA + small chevron that focuses the timeline entry.
lina: Figma note: add a focused state for the anchored timeline row and a 160ms scroll-to animation. Include reduced-motion variant that jumps instead.
maya: A11y: when the toast CTA opens the timeline, SR should announce "Timeline opened: version 47 rolled back by @ryan, two minutes ago". Use aria-live=polite for toast, and the timeline panel heading should be aria-live=assertive only when opened via toast CTA.
devon: Copy suggestions for toast: A) "Rollback applied 1: view history" B) "Rolled back to v47 1: view history". I prefer B for immediate context.
joan: Let's standardize to: "Rolled back to v{version} 1% traffic | View history" but hide the percent when it's 100% to keep it concise.marta: small nit: change the canary control label from 'Pause' to 'Pause new traffic' in the control tooltip and ARIA label to reduce ambiguity.
lina: I'll update frames and include the chevron micro-interaction.
maya: I'll add SR strings and checklist for timestamp humanization and tooltip with full ISO time.
devon: I'll PR the copy and add unit tests for the undo aria-label.
designbot: Actions: update toast copy, add deep-link anchor (#history:id), timeline focus state token, motion variants, a11y announce strings, change canary tooltip.
joan: Thanks team 1; I'll link the updated figma later.
